items.title: German Chancellor Merz calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on
items.description: Exit polls show damaging losses for Merz's centre-right CDU party in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin.

items.title: Russia's elections had few surprises - but how the Kremlin uses the results will be crucial
items.description: Vladimir Putin will likely use the result to claim most Russians back the so-called special military operation in Ukraine, writes the BBC's Steve Rosenberg.

items.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico to file lawsuit against Trump's White House ban
items.description: The US media outlets say they are defending "the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes".

items.title: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
items.description: The groups have been active in Ethiopia's most populous regions for years and now say they will work together.

items.title: US strikes on alleged drug boats could be crimes against humanity, says UN
items.description: A report says the attacks, of which there have been at least 68, were not self-defence.

items.title: British Museum bans visitors from photographing Bayeux Tapestry
items.description: Visitors stopping to take pictures of the 68m medieval embroidery were holding up others, prompting the rule change.

items.title: Three arrested in South Africa over one of nine women's body finds
items.description: The body of Jabulile Ntimba was the ninth to be found recently in an area east of Johannesburg.

items.title: Jailed teacher convicted of sexual abuse secretly released early in Indonesia, BBC finds
items.description: Undercover footage recorded by the BBC reveals he has been released after serving less than half his sentence.

items.title: US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit
items.description: Top US and Chinese officials held talks in New York on Sunday ahead of a Trump-Xi summit this week.

items.title: UK should 'team up' with Canada in new Europe alliance, Canadian minister tells BBC
items.description: It comes after European Commission President proposed "opening the door" for Canada to become an associate member of the EU.

items.title: Presley Gerber, Cindy Crawford's son, dies aged 27
items.description: His family asked for privacy during a "very difficult and painful time" following the model's death.

items.title: Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband says he forgave her so he would not be 'eaten up inside forever'
items.description: Patrick Clancy gives his first interview since his wife's mistrial over the killing of their three young children.

items.title: Sydney policeman allegedly disguised himself as Uber Eats rider before murders
items.description: Beaumont Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to the 2024 murder of his ex-partner and his new boyfriend.

items.title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting
items.description: While Burnham praised the agreement, Lib Dem leader Ed Davey called it a "pretend" victory for Trump.

items.title: Houthis say they targeted Saudi capital with ballistic missiles
items.description: A reported strike on a fuel depot at Riyadh airport caused delays on Saturday, as Saudi Arabia says it shot down a ballistic missile aimed at the capital.

items.title: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says
items.description: Moscow's mayor says 450 drones were downed during the overnight barrage, in which two people died.

items.title: Sister of Pakistan's ex-PM Imran Khan arrested
items.description: Aleema Khanum is accused of mobilising her brother’s supporters ahead of country-wide protests.

items.title: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex with drones and snipers
items.description: Trump said the updated plans were at the request of the US military and for national security purposes.

items.title: Inside Djibouti refugee camp for thousands fleeing Houthi advance in Yemen
items.description: Fighting on Yemen's west coast has prompted thousands of people to flee by boat across the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

items.title: Workers came across human remains – and unearthed a mass grave of 572 people
items.description: Workers in northern Sri Lanka accidentally uncovered the country's largest mass grave – and reopened wounds from its civil war.
